newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Mercosur chiefs laud pace of economic integration.
newsitem.headline: Mercosur chiefs laud pace of economic integration.

text.p: The presidents of the four countries in the Mercosur trade bloc closed a one-day summit in Brazil on Tuesday, promising to keep up the speedy pace of economic integration among the group's members.
The South American leaders said the linking of their economies was proceeding faster than integration within NAFTA.
Speaking at a joint news conference, the presidents said Mecrosur had won the respect of the international community and was being recognized as an "emerging economic power."

"Mercosur has a level of internal integration far greater than that of NAFTA," said Argentine President Carlos Menem, referring to the North American Free Trade Agreement, which links Canada, Mexico and the United States.
Menem's remark was received with applause by his colleagues from Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay and the leaders of Chile and Bolivia, who joined them at the meeting.

Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso described Mercosur as a "training ground" for a proposed free trade agreement to which virtually all countries in the continent have made commitments to join by 2005.
Cardoso dismissed criticism that Mercosur was a closed trade group and that it was growing at the expense of the development of its trade with outside countries.
"The results are in the figures," he said, adding that Mercosur trade with third countries had more than doubled to $59 billion since the group was launched five years ago.
The presidents lauded the signing of a free trade agreement with Bolivia, which follows Chile as the second country to seek closer economic ties with Mercosur.
